whatChanged.title: Climate coverage remained mainstream but became more transmission-focused
whatChanged.detail: Insurance, adaptation, and infrastructure language appeared alongside emissions and weather framing.

whyItMatters.summary: Climate becomes more decision-useful when the theme moves from abstract awareness into financing, insurance, infrastructure, and policy transmission.
statements: Pure weather coverage is weaker than repeated evidence of pricing, regulation, and adaptation investment.
The theme should be treated as structural when multiple sectors inherit the consequences.

requiredClaims: The brief should cite non-weather transmission, such as insurance repricing or infrastructure adaptation.
At least one policy or institutional evidence lane should support the quarter.
provenanceExpectations: Use aggregate theme movement for persistence and curated items for consequence framing.
notes: Do not reduce climate to a weather digest.

subtopicMovement.rationale: Financial transmission signals are becoming more visible.
Infrastructure and resilience narratives make the theme more actionable.

pathways.note: Reinsurers often show whether climate risk is becoming operationally priced.
Transition and grid investment can create indirect exposure pathways.

risks.title: Storm headline bias
risks.detail: Disaster coverage can inflate urgency without proving structural transmission.

watchpoints.trigger: Insurance, grid, and policy evidence all remain active
watchpoints.implication: Confidence rises that the theme is broadening beyond awareness into capital allocation.

prompts: Which climate subtheme is producing the clearest economic transmission signal this quarter?

notes: This file exists to keep climate briefs consequence-oriented rather than headline-oriented.
